jobs.title: PhD Fellow in Arctic Mobility, Landscape and Spatial Justice
jobs.employer: UNIVERSITETET I TROMSØ - NORGES ARKTISKE UNIVERSITET UIT CAMPUS TROMSØ
jobs.description:
The position

At The School of Business and Economics at UiT The Arctic University of Norway, ROADS is seeking a highly motivated doctoral researcher interested in questions of mobility, infrastructure, northern landscapes, environmental change, and spatial justice in the Arctic. The successful applicant will become part of an interdisciplinary research team combining geography, environmental humanities, Indigenous studies, critical infrastructure studies, heritage research, and spatial analysis. The PhD position is funded for three years, starting 1 March 2027 and ending 28 February 2030, and is embedded within an international and collaborative research environment.

The objective of the position is to complete research training to the level of a doctoral degree. Admission to the PhD programme is a prerequisite for employment, and the programme period starts on commencement of the position.

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.

Working and living in Tromsø 

Tromsø/Romssa serves as an important hub for research, culture, governance, and mobility in the region of Northern Norway and Sápmi. Its position as a regional gateway between coastal, inland, and cross-border northern landscapes makes it a particularly meaningful base for ROADS. The School of Business and Economics at UiT hosts a growing community of scholars working on sustainability, governance, mobilities, Arctic transformations, and societal change. The successful candidate will become part of a dynamic interdisciplinary environment, including UiT’s Environmental Humanities thematic network that ROADS is closely connected to. 


The project

ROADS offers the first systematic study of residual road infrastructures in Northern Fennoscandia—roads and pathways that have fallen out of official purpose but continue to shape landscapes, memories, and mobility practices across the region. These include bypassed roads, abandoned transport corridors, former military and extractive infrastructures, and old roads and seasonal pathways embedded within local and Sámi land-use traditions.

While many remain visible in the landscape, their histories increasingly persist through local knowledge systems that risk disappearing as generations pass. Rather than approaching such infrastructures as obsolete remnants, ROADS conceptualizes them as living archives: material traces through which memory, power, mobility, resistance, and future possibilities continue to unfold.

Drawing on feminist and decolonial Science and Technology Studies, critical infrastructure studies, political ecology, environmental humanities and Indigenous ontologies, ROADS seeks to broaden conventional understandings of infrastructure by integrating relational, seasonal, and more-than human mobility systems into analyses of northern landscapes.

The project combines GIS-based spatial analysis, archival research, ethnography, repeat photography and artistic methods, and collaborative countermapping. It is grounded in close collaboration with local and Sámi communities and culminates in community-responsive public outputs, including a multilingual digital storymap and participatory mapping platform.

While GIS and spatial analysis provide important analytical foundations, ROADS combines these approaches with ethnographic, archival, visual, and artistic methods. The project therefore welcomes applicants interested in methodological experimentation and interdisciplinary research across the social sciences, humanities, environmental sciences, and arts. 


The PhD project, responsibilities and research methods

The PhD project and responsibilities

The successful candidate will undertake doctoral research mainly within Work Package 2: Mapping Conflict and Relational Mobility in the North. The PhD candidate will take a leading role in the WP and receive close supervision from the Principal Investigator while collaborating with the project's postdoctoral researcher and the project network.

The PhD project explores how contemporary road development in Northern Fennoscandia—including infrastructure connected to resource extraction, military activities, and regional development—interacts with older roads, seasonal pathways, and Indigenous and local mobility systems. Rather than treating infrastructure as fixed physical objects, the PhD project investigates roads as dynamic political, cultural, and material assemblages that shape relationships between people, landscapes, governance, and more-than-human worlds. 

Particular attention is given to questions such as: 

  • How do expanding road infrastructures interact with Indigenous and local land use, seasonal mobilities, and relational understandings of landscape? 
  • How are access, mobility, and territorial authority negotiated between different actors, including local communities, Sámi reindeer herders, planners, governmental agencies, and extractive industries?
  • How do roads simultaneously enable, constrain, and transform relationships between people and northern landscapes?

The PhD candidate will have the opportunity to shape the detailed direction of the dissertation within the broader aims of the project. 

Research methods

The project combines: 

  • Archival research
  • GIS and spatial analysis
  • Participatory and critical mapping
  • Ethnographic fieldwork
  • Walking interviews
  • Policy analysis
  • Visual and spatial storytelling 

GIS analysis forms an important component of the project, but it is integrated with qualitative, participatory, and community-engaged approaches. The project therefore welcomes applicants interested in combining spatial analysis with ethnographic and critical social science methods. Fieldwork will involve collaboration with local residents, Sámi communities, municipal planners, land users, and other stakeholders across Northern Fennoscandia.

Applicants are required to submit a project description (3–5 pages, literature references included) outlining how they would approach the proposed doctoral research within Work Package 2 of ROADS. The project description should demonstrate the applicant's understanding of the aims of ROADS and discuss how they would investigate questions related to infrastructure, mobility, landscape, territorial governance, and Indigenous and local land use in Northern Fennoscandia.

While the dissertation is situated within Work Package 2, applicants are encouraged to develop their own research focus within the overall objectives of the project. The final project description will be developed in cooperation with the supervisor. 

The description should reflect on relevant theoretical perspectives and methodological approaches appropriate for doctoral research. Applicants are encouraged to discuss how methods such as GIS and spatial analysis, participatory and critical mapping, ethnographic fieldwork, archival and policy analysis, visual methods, and interdisciplinary collaboration could contribute to their proposed research. The proposal does not need to include all of these approaches but should demonstrate thoughtful consideration of the methods most appropriate for the applicant's intended doctoral project. Applicants should also indicate how their academic background, research interests, and methodological competencies would contribute to the interdisciplinary research environment of ROADS while supporting the development of an original doctoral dissertation. 


Contact

For further information about the position and the ROADS project, please contact: 

Dr. Tarja Salmela, Principal Investigator, ROADS
School of Business and Economics, BFE UiT The Arctic University of Norway

Email: tarja.t.salmela@uit.no 


Qualifications

Required qualifications: 

  • Applicants must hold a Master's degree equivalent to a Norwegian Master's degree in geography, human geography, Indigenous studies, environmental humanities, archaeology, anthropology, planning, GIScience, landscape studies, political ecology, heritage studies, environmental studies, digital humanities, or another relevant discipline. Qualification with a master’s degree is required before commencement in the position. You may still apply if you are in the final stages of the master’s degree, but the master’s thesis must be submitted for evaluation within the application deadline. You must submit the thesis and transcripts of grades for the master's degree with your application. 
  • Strong academic performance and collaboration skills.
  • Proficiency in spoken and written English. Nordic applicants can document their English capabilities by attaching their high school diploma. 
  • Demonstrated interest in Arctic, Indigenous, environmental, mobility, infrastructure, or landscape research. 
  • Ability to work independently while contributing actively to collaborative research.

Desired qualifications: 

  • Archival or historical research.
  • GIS and spatial analysis. 
  • Critical GIS, participatory mapping, or countermapping. 
  • Qualitative or ethnographic research. • Indigenous methodologies and community-based research. 
  • Political ecology, infrastructure studies, environmental humanities, or mobility studies. 
  • Visual methods, digital storytelling, or creative and arts-based research.
  • Skills in Norwegian, Swedish, Finnish, or a Sámi language

We also value applicants who are motivated to develop language skills relevant to the project's geographical and cultural contexts. Applicants with backgrounds in geography, archaeology, digital heritage, landscape studies, environmental humanities, Indigenous studies, anthropology, planning, and related disciplines are particularly encouraged to apply. ROADS is grounded in long-term collaboration with local and Sámi communities and engages critically with Indigenous knowledge systems and questions of self-determination and cultural heritage. We encourage applications from researchers whose experiences and perspectives can contribute to the project's commitment to plurality, community engagement, and inclusive knowledge production.

In the assessment, the emphasis is on the applicant's potential to complete a research education based on the master's thesis or equivalent, and any other scientific work. The project description will also be considered. In addition, professional experience and other experience of significance for the completion of the doctoral programme will be taken into consideration.

We will also emphasize motivation and personal suitability for the position. We are looking for candidates who:

  • Have good collaboration skills
  • Have good communication and interaction with colleagues and students
  • Wants to contribute to a good working environment

As many people as possible should have the opportunity to undertake organized research training. If you already hold a PhD or have equivalent competence, we will not appoint you to this position.


Admission to the PhD programme 

For employment in the PhD position, you must be qualified for admission to the PhD programme at the Faculty of Biosciences, Fisheries and Economics and participate in organized doctoral studies within the employment period.

Admission normally requires:  

  • A bachelor's degree of 180 ECTS and a master's degree of 120 ECTS, or an integrated master's degree of 300 ECTS. 
  • A master's thesis with a scope corresponding to at least 30 ECTS for a master's degree of 120 ECTS. 
  • A master's thesis with a scope corresponding to at least 20 ECTS for an integrated master's degree of 300 ECTS. 

Grade requirements applies both to the master thesis as well as courses part of the master’s degree. The minimum requirements are grade B or better on the master’s degree, and an average grade of B or better on courses that are part of the master’s degree. For integrated master's degrees, applicants are required to have achieved a grade of B or higher on their master's thesis and an overall average grade of C or higher across all courses comprising the integrated degree programme. A more detailed description of admission requirements can be found here.  

If you are employed in the position, you will be provisionally admitted to the PhD programme. Application for final admission must be submitted no later than two months after taking up the position. 

Applicants with a foreign education will be subjected to an evaluation of whether the educational background is equal to Norwegian higher education, following national guidelines from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills. Depending on which country the education is from, one or two additional years of university education may be required to fulfil admission requirements, e.g. a 4-year bachelor's degree and a 2-year master's degree. UiT normally accepts higher education from countries that are part of the Lisbon Recognition Convention.


Inclusion and diversity

UiT The Arctic University of Norway is working actively to promote equality, gender balance and diversity among employees and students, and to create an inclusive and safe working environment. We believe that inclusion and diversity are a strength, and we want employees with different competencies, professional experience, life experience and perspectives.

If you have a disability, a gap in your CV or immigrant background, we encourage you to tick the box for this in your application. If there are qualified applicants, we invite at least one in each group for an interview. If you get the job, we will adapt the working conditions if you need it. Apart from selecting the right candidates, we will only use the information for anonymous statistics.


We offer

The successful candidate will join an internationally connected and intellectually vibrant research environment at UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Handelshøgskolen, and the thematic network of Environmental Humanities at UiT. The successful candidate will become part of an innovative research project addressing pressing questions concerning infrastructure, mobility, cultural heritage, and environmental change in the Arctic.

  • The opportunity to contribute to a research project with strong academic and societal relevance
  • Close collaboration with researchers working across Arctic studies, mobility studies, infrastructure studies, environmental humanities, Indigenous studies, heritage research, and critical geography
  • Opportunities for international collaboration, conference participation, publication, and career development
  • Access to GIS and research infrastructure through UiT
  • Good career opportunities 
  • Flexible working hours and a state collective pay agreement  
  • Pension scheme through the state pension fund 
  • The remuneration for the position is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1017 with a gross annual salary ranging from NOK 580 000 to 600 000 (in a 100% position), with a 3% yearly increase

Norwegian health policy aims to ensure that everyone, irrespective of their personal finances and where they live, has access to good health and care services of equal standard. As an employee you will become member of the National Insurance Scheme which also include health care services.

More practical information about working and living in Norway can be found here: https://uit.no/staffmobility


Application 

Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information submitted by the application deadline via Jobbnorge. It is therefore important that you include all necessary documents demonstrating your qualifications for the position.

Your application must include: 

  • Cover letter explaining your motivation and research interests
  • Academic CV
  • Official diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language 
  • Official transcripts of grades/academic record for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language
  • Official translation of diplomas and transcripts of records (ToR) to English or a Scandinavian language, if applicable
  • Explanation of the grading system for foreign education (Diploma Supplement if available)
  • Documentation of English proficiency
  • Documentation of proficiency in Norwegian (or a Scandinavian language) (if available)
  • References with contact information
  • Master’s thesis, and any other academic works
  • Publication list (if available)
  • Project description (3-5 pages)

Qualification with a master’s degree is required before commencement in the position. You may still apply if you are in the final stages of the master’s degree, but the master’s thesis must be submitted for evaluation within the application deadline. You must submit the thesis and transcript of grades for the master’s degree with your application.

All documentation to be considered must be in a Scandinavian language or English. If English proficiency is not documented in the application, it must be documented before starting in the position. 


Assessment 

The applicants will be assessed by an expert committee. The committee's mandate is to undertake an assessment of the applicants' qualifications based on the written material presented by the applicants, and the detailed description draw up for the position. A copy of the assessment report will be sent to all applicants. 

The applicants who are assessed as best qualified will be called to an interview. The interview should among other things, aim to clarify the applicant’s motivation and personal suitability for the position. 


General information 

The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants. 

Remuneration for the position of PhD Fellow is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1017. A compulsory contribution of 2 % to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted. You will become a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, which gives you many benefits in addition to a lifelong pension: You may be entitled to financial support if you become ill or disabled, your family may be entitled to financial support when you die, you become insured against occupational injury or occupational disease, and you can get good terms on a mortgage. Read more about your employee benefits at: spk.no.

A shorter period of appointment may be decided when the PhD Fellow has already completed parts of their research training programme or when the appointment is based on a previous qualifying position PhD Fellow, research assistant, or the like in such a way that the total time used for research training amounts to three years. 

We process personal data given in an application or CV in accordance with the Personal Data Act (Offentleglova). According to the Personal Data Act information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure. You will receive advance notification in the event of such publication, if you have requested non-disclosure. 


Om arbeidsgiveren:

UiT The Arctic University of Norway is a multi-campus research university and the northernmost university of the world. Our central location in the High North, our broad and diverse research and study portfolio, and our interdisciplinary qualities make us uniquely suited to meet the challenges of the future. At UiT you can explore global issues from a close-up perspective.

Credibility, academic freedom, closeness, creativity and commitment shall be hallmarks of the relationship between our employees, between our employees and our students and between UiT and our partners. 

The Faculty of Biosciences, Fisheries and Economics (BFE) consists of Department of Arctic and Marine Biology, Norwegian College of Fishery Science (NFH) and School of Business and Economics.The main task of BFE is to conduct teaching and research dissemination at a high national and international level within all relevant fields. Prioritized research areas are aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, climate, life in the arctic, marine bioprospecting, fish health, seafood products, business and macroeconomics, resources and environment, markets and management of marine resources. The interdisciplinary profile of the faculty provides good opportunity to develop research projects involving several research groups at the faculty according to its strategy.

These include bypassed roads, abandoned transport corridors, former military and extractive infrastructures, and old roads and seasonal pathways embedded within local and Sámi land-use traditions.

While many remain visible in the landscape, their histories increasingly persist through local knowledge systems that risk disappearing as generations pass. Rather than approaching such infrastructures as obsolete remnants, ROADS conceptualizes them as living archives: material traces through which memory, power, mobility, resistance, and future possibilities continue to unfold.

Drawing on feminist and decolonial Science and Technology Studies, critical infrastructure studies, political ecology, environmental humanities and Indigenous ontologies, ROADS seeks to broaden conventional understandings of infrastructure by integrating relational, seasonal, and more-than human mobility systems into analyses of northern landscapes.

The project combines GIS-based spatial analysis, archival research, ethnography, repeat photography and artistic methods, and collaborative countermapping. The postdoctoral project and responsibilities

The Postdoctoral Research Fellow will play a central role in the project and contribute to both its analytical and public-facing outputs.

The postdoctoral researcher will lead the spatial and archival components of Work Package 1: Tracing the temporal lives of residual and rendered invisible infrastructures and contribute to synthesis and engagement activities in Work Package 3: Reimagining residual road infrastructures and mobilities in Northern Fennoscandia.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Conducting GIS-based spatial analysis of residual road infrastructures across Northern Fennoscandia.
  • Integrating historical maps, infrastructure records, aerial imagery, and satellite data to identify and visualize infrastructural change over time.
  • Developing innovative approaches to critical spatial visualization and mapping that foreground questions of memory, erasure, survivance, and infrastructural power.
  • Contributing to archival research and the interpretation of historical infrastructure records.
  • Participating in ethnographic fieldwork, collaborative mapping activities, repeat photography, and visual documentation initiatives alongside the Principal Investigator.
  • Co-leading participatory countermapping workshops and contributing to the development of a multilingual digital storymap and other public facing outputs.
  • Publishing research findings in leading international journals and contributing to conferences, outreach activities, and project dissemination.

The position offers an opportunity to engage with northern landscapes and communities across Northern Fennoscandia in a place-sensitive way. Fieldwork will take place in active collaboration with local and Sámi knowledge holders and cultural institutions. The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to research that is attentive to the diverse histories, experiences, and knowledge systems that shape northern mobility landscapes.

The postdoctoral researcher will work closely with the Principal Investigator while also developing an independent research profile within the broader framework of the project.

  • Skills in Norwegian, Swedish, Finnish, or a Sámi language are considered an asset. We also value applicants who are motivated to develop language skills relevant to the project's geographical and cultural contexts.
  • Experience with critical GIS, participatory mapping, countermapping, or spatial humanities approaches.
  • Knowledge of Arctic, Northern, Indigenous, environmental, infrastructure, mobility, landscape, or heritage research.
  • Experience integrating qualitative and quantitative spatial methods.
  • Skills in visual storytelling, cartographic design, digital heritage, digital humanities, or multimedia research dissemination.
  • Experience conducting archival research and working with historical sources.
  • Interest in interdisciplinary and creative research methods, including visual, arts-based, or experimental approaches to landscape and infrastructure research.
  • Experience working across disciplinary boundaries and integrating spatial, archival, ethnographic, visual, or participatory methods.
  • Familiarity with community-based research, collaborative knowledge production, and Indigenous methodologies

ROADS is grounded in long-term collaboration with local and Sámi communities and engages critically with Indigenous knowledge systems and questions of self-determination and cultural heritage. Sámi scholars and other Indigenous scholars, as well as applicants with relevant experience working in Indigenous research contexts, are particularly encouraged to apply. We also encourage applications from researchers whose experiences and perspectives can contribute to the project's commitment to plurality, community engagement, and inclusive knowledge production.

In the assessment the main emphasis will be attached to the submitted works and the project proposal for the qualifying work. Emphasis shall also be attached to experience from popularization/dissemination and academic policy and administrative activity.

During the assessment emphasis will be put on the candidate’s motivation, potential for research, and personal suitability for the position. We are looking for candidates who:

  • Have good collaboration skills
  • Have good communication and interaction with colleagues and students
  • Wants to contribute to a good working environment

At UiT we put emphasis on the quality, relevance and significance of the research work and not on where the work is published, in accordance with the principles of The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).

Inclusion and diversity

UiT The Arctic University i Norway is working actively to promote equality, gender balance and diversity among employees and students, and to create an inclusive and safe working environment. We believe that inclusion and diversity is a strength, and we want employees with different competencies, professional experience, life experience and perspectives.

If you have a disability, a gap in your CV or immigrant background, we encourage you to tick the box for this in your application. If there are qualified applicants, we invite least one in each group for an interview. If you get the job, we will adapt the working conditions if you need it. Apart from selecting the right candidates, we will only use the information for anonymous statistics.

We offer

The successful candidate will join an internationally connected and intellectually vibrant research environment at UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Handelshøgskolen, and the thematic network of Environmental Humanities at UiT. The successful candidate will become part of an innovative research project addressing pressing questions concerning infrastructure, mobility, cultural heritage, and environmental change in the Arctic.

The position offers:

  • The opportunity to contribute to a research project with strong academic and societal relevance.
  • Close collaboration with researchers working across Arctic studies, mobility studies, infrastructure studies, environmental humanities, Indigenous studies, heritage research, and critical geography.
  • Opportunities for international collaboration, conference participation, publication, and career development.
  • Access to GIS and research infrastructure through UiT.
  • Significant opportunities to develop a strong academic research profile.
  • Good career opportunities 
  • Flexible working hours and a state collective pay agreement
  • Pension scheme through the state pension fund

Norwegian health policy aims to ensure that everyone, irrespective of their personal finances and where they live, has access to good health and care services of equal standard. As an employee you will become member of the National Insurance Scheme which also include health care services.

More practical information for working and living in Norway can be found here: https://uit.no/staffmobility

Application

Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information submitted by the application deadline via Jobbnorge. It is therefore important that you include all necessary documents demonstrating your qualifications for the position.

Your application must include:

  • Letter of motivation
  • Project proposal (3–5 pages)
  • Academic CV
  • Diplomas and transcripts (all degrees)
  • Documentation of English proficiency
  • Contact information to 2-3 references
  • Documentation of educational competence, if available
  • Description of your academic production, stating which works you consider most important
  • Publication list
  • Academic works, up to ten. The doctoral thesis is regarded as one work.

If you’re at the final stages of your PhD, you may still apply if you have submitted your PhD thesis for doctoral degree evaluation within the application deadline. You must submit the thesis with your application. Documentation of your completed PhD degree must be submitted before commencement.

All documentation to be considered must be in a Scandinavian language or English. If English proficiency is not documented in the application, it must be documented before starting in the position.

Assessment

The applicants will be assessed by an expert committee. The committee's mandate is to undertake an assessment of the applicants' qualifications based on the written material presented by the applicants, and the detailed description draw up for the position. A copy of the assessment report will be sent to all applicants.

The applicants who are assessed as best qualified will be called to an interview. The interview should among other things, aim to clarify the applicant’s motivation and personal suitability for the position. A trial lecture may also be held.

General information

The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants.

The remuneration for Postdoctoral research fellow is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1352 with a gross annual salary ranging from NOK 630 000 to 720 000 (in a 100% position). (In special cases, a higher salary may be considered.) A compulsory contribution of 2 % to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted. You will become a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, which gives you many benefits in addition to a lifelong pension. Read more about your employee benefits at: spk.no.

The successful candidate must be willing to get involved in the ongoing development of their department and the university as a whole.

UiT wishes to promote gender equality. If two or more applicants are found to be equally qualified, the university will rank applicants from the underrepresented gender ahead of others.

According to the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act (Offentleglova) information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

UiT The Arctic University of Norway is a multi-campus research university and the northernmost university of the world. Our central location in the High North, our broad and diverse research and study portfolio, and our interdisciplinary qualities make us uniquely suited to meet the challenges of the future. At UiT you can explore global issues from a close-up perspective.

Credibility, academic freedom, closeness, creativity and commitment shall be hallmarks of the relationship between our employees, between our employees and our students and between UiT and our partners. 

The Faculty of Biosciences, Fisheries and Economics (BFE) consists of Department of Arctic and Marine Biology, Norwegian College of Fishery Science (NFH) and School of Business and Economics.The main task of BFE is to conduct teaching and research dissemination at a high national and international level within all relevant fields. Prioritized research areas are aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, climate, life in the arctic, marine bioprospecting, fish health, seafood products, business and macroeconomics, resources and environment, markets and management of marine resources. The interdisciplinary profile of the faculty provides good opportunity to develop research projects involving several research groups at the faculty according to its strategy.

Join H&M Group in a high-impact role where you’ll shape how store space is planned, measured and optimised across markets. As our Retail Space Planning Expert, you’ll turn data into smart strategies that improve productivity across our store portfolio, influence retail design and help create better customer experiences at scale.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

As a Retail Space Planning Expert, you define and execute strategies that optimise store space productivity across formats. WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH

You’ll work closely with Retail  Design, Retail tech, Commercial, Assortment, Retail Space and Sales Market teams. You collaborate with business and tech stakeholders to ensure space strategies are practical, scalable and consistently executed.



WHO YOU ARE

We are looking for people with…

    A relevant degree in Business Administration, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent work experience
    5+ years of experience in retail strategy development and implementation for commercial space
    Experience leading large, complex projects from start to end, developing business strategies or solutions in a retail environment across business and tech stakeholders
    Experience working with space and assortment-related data, store layouts and store design teams
    Experience working with assortment composition for commercial or retail spaces

And people who are…

    Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex data into simple, actionable insights
    High attention to detail and strong communication skills
    Strong stakeholder management and collaboration abilities
    Ability to balance operational detail with a strategic perspective



WHO WE ARE

H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make.

We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we use our power, our scale and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future.



WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE

At H&M Group, we are proud to be a vibrant and welcoming company. We offer our employees attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe.

    A role with strong influence on store performance and space productivity at scale

JOIN US

Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things — our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are.

Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here.

jobs.title: Project & Business Coordinator
jobs.description:
Avincis is looking for a Project & Business Coordinator to join our Nordic organisation. This is a broad and highly collaborative role where you will work closely with our Nordic management team and colleagues across Sweden, Norway, Finland and Denmark. 

You will be at the centre of projects, business improvement initiatives and management activities that span functions and countries. From coordinating strategic projects and Management of Change processes to supporting business cases, contracts and performance reporting, you will help ensure that priorities move forward and that decisions are translated into action. 

For the right person, this is an excellent opportunity to gain broad exposure to a complex, international aviation business and work closely with senior management.

Location: Stockholm, Tromsø or Esbjerg

Reports to: Managing Director Nordics



The role

As our Project & Business Coordinator, you will support and coordinate strategic initiatives and cross-functional projects across the Nordic organisation. 

You will bring structure, follow-up and momentum to projects and business activities, while also supporting the Nordic management team with analysis, reporting, contracts and decision-making material. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

  • Coordinating cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives across the Nordics 
  • Developing and maintaining project plans, milestones, budgets, risk registers and progress reporting 
  • Coordinating Management of Change (MOC) processes and ensuring appropriate documentation and follow-up 
  • Supporting the preparation of business cases, investment proposals and cost-saving initiatives 
  • Facilitating project meetings, workshops and steering group meetings and following up agreed actions 
  • Supporting contract administration, negotiations, renewals and amendments 
  • Supporting commercial activities and tender processes 
  • Preparing management reports, presentations and decision-making material 
  • Analysing operational and financial performance and supporting KPI and dashboard reporting 
  • Identifying opportunities to improve, simplify and standardise processes across the Nordic organisation 
  • Supporting strategic planning, organisational development and change initiatives 
  • Acting as a connecting point between management, operational teams and support functions across countries 
Who are we looking for?

We believe you are a structured and proactive person who enjoys working in an environment where priorities can change and where collaboration is essential. 

You are comfortable coordinating several activities at the same time and know how to create clarity and progress without losing sight of the bigger picture. You enjoy working with people across different functions and levels of an organisation and are confident interacting with senior stakeholders. 

You probably have experience from project coordination, project management, business support, business development or a similar role. 

We would also like you to have: 

  • Strong organisational and project management or coordination skills 
  • An understanding of financial analysis and business cases 
  • Good analytical and problem-solving capabilities 
  • Experience or understanding of contract administration and commercial processes 
  • An understanding of risk management and governance 
  • Strong communication skills in English and at least one Nordic language 
  • Experience supporting management teams and senior stakeholders 
  • Experience from aviation or another regulated industry, tender or procurement processes, Management of Change and/or SAP is an advantage, but not a requirement.

What will make you successful? 

You are someone who takes ownership and makes things happen. You enjoy creating structure where there are many moving parts, following up on actions and ensuring that projects continue to move forward. 

At the same time, you are curious about the business behind the projects. You want to understand why we are doing something, not just what needs to be done. 

You are collaborative, pragmatic and comfortable working across different countries, functions and cultures. 

Why join Avincis?

At Avincis, our work has a clear purpose. We provide critical aviation services across Europe, supporting missions where aviation makes a real difference. 

In this role, you will have the opportunity to work across our Nordic organisation and gain insight into many different parts of the business. You will work closely with Nordic management while collaborating with colleagues in operations, finance, safety, HR, procurement and other functions. 

It is a role with broad exposure, significant variety and the opportunity to influence how we work across the Nordics. 

If you are looking for a role where you can combine projects, business, analysis and collaboration – and where no two days are quite the same – we would love to hear from you. 

Ready to take the next step? Apply and become part of Avincis Nordics.

jobs.title: Research Assistant Positions in Development of AI-based Decision Support
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for two part-time research assistant positions with SDU Health Informatics and Technology (HIT), The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI), University of Southern Denmark (SDU), Odense. Both positions are for 1 years at 25% (9,25 hours/week). The planned starting date for the positions is October 1, 2026.

 

Tasks

Both research assistant positions will focus on development of AI-based decision support. One position will be related to a joint project with Hospital Sønderjylland (Sønderborg) on personalized cardiovascular risk prediction and diagnostic support for patients with advanced kidney disease. The other position will be related to a joint project with Lillebælt Hospital (Vejle) on detection of smoking status and symptoms for lung cancer patients.

 

Ideal candidates

To qualify for the positions, you must hold a M.Sc. degree in software engineering, artificial intelligence, computer science, or a related discipline.

The ideal candidates will have many of the following competences.

  • artificial intelligence experience (including explainability and interpretability)

  • experience in development of AI-augmented decision support tools

  • experience in interdisciplinary work

  • experience in working with external stakeholders and domain experts

  • knowledge of the health domain

 

About MMMI and SDU HIT

MMMI is an internationally recognized research department that conducts research within robotics, drone technology, artificial intelligence, I4.0, software engineering as well as health and energy informatics.

SDU HIT conducts interdisciplinary research related to data driven health technology in close collaboration with experts from various fields. There is a strong emphasis on the development of high TRL systems related to intelligent monitoring and decision support; predictive models for prevention, early detection, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis; digital health systems offering novel personalized data collection, treatment plans and interventions. SDU HIT has research activities in areas such as geriatrics, mental health, compassion, cancer, cardiology, kidney disease, osteoporosis, and multiple sclerosis.

 

Additional information

For further information about the positions, please contact Professor Uffe Kock Wiil, phone +45 6011 3565, email ukwiil@mmmi.sdu.dk.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

  • Motivated application.

  • Curriculum Vitae. 

  • Master’s and Bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (original and an official English translation). 

  • Complete list of publications, if you have any.

  • Publications most relevant for the position (max. 2).

  • A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is August 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation.

Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms
This appointment as a research assistant is part-time and temporary for an initial 1-year period, and the preferred start date is from October 1, 2026. Extension may be possible depending on available funding. 

Employment as a research assistant requires qualifications at minimum master’s level (equivalent to a Danish master’s degree) at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for research assistant as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

jobs.title: Postdoc Positions in Autonomous Drone Flight in Confined Spaces for Wind Turbine Inspection
jobs.description:
The SDU UAS Center, part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, invites applications for one or more postdoc positions on autonomous flight in confined and cluttered environments for multi-rotor drones. The positions are for a two-year employment with a flexible start date.

 

What We Offer
The successful candidates will become part of the SDU UAS Center, where we conduct cutting-edge research in civilian drone technologies and future drone applications in critical sectors, such as agriculture, inspection, energy, and healthcare. At the heart of our mission is the creation of groundbreaking drone solutions that address key societal challenges. We are committed to fostering a dynamic and inspiring work environment where creativity flourishes. We often collaborate closely with world-leading companies, some of which are part of the vibrant robotic startup community around Odense.

The positions are tied to the development of an Automated Service Inspection (ASI) system for wind turbines, carried out in close collaboration with Vestas. Wind energy is a cornerstone of the green transition, yet the industry depends heavily on manual inspections and a shrinking pool of service technicians. Autonomous drones that can fly safely inside and around turbine structures are a key enabler for scalable, data-driven maintenance, promising less downtime, improved safety, and higher energy production across a growing global fleet.

 

Work Area
The successful candidates will conduct research and development within autonomous flight in confined spaces, where safety and robustness under real-world conditions are paramount. Flying close to and inside turbine structures, such as the tower interior, raises fundamental research challenges: navigation without reliable GNSS, perception in geometrically complex environments, and safe motion planning within centimetres of critical infrastructure. Concretely, the work will include the following:

  • State estimation and localisation in GNSS-denied, confined environments (visual-inertial odometry (VIO), simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM), sensor fusion).

  • Real-time perception.

  • Motion planning and control for safe, agile flight in close proximity to obstacles and infrastructure.

  • Prototyping of drones and payloads tailored to confined-space inspection, from concept and mechanical/electronics integration to flight-ready platforms.

  • Integration of autonomy with onboard inspection payloads (cameras, microphones) and existing turbine data.

  • Operation and flight testing of multi-rotor UAS, including experiments at turbine sites.

During the appointment, the successful candidates will also have the opportunity to work on related autonomy challenges across the center’s project portfolio, where autonomous flight under demanding real-world conditions is a recurring theme.

The positions may involve co-supervising related student projects. The candidates will be part of the SDU UAS Center and are expected to participate in the center's project portfolio and outreach activities.

 

We Expect

We expect that you hold a PhD degree or expect to be awarded one before the start date, within engineering, robotics, computer science, or another related field. You do not need to cover every area below, but you should have experience with, and a genuine interest in, some of the following:

  • Research and development within autonomous navigation, state estimation, or motion planning for robots or UAS.

  • Research and development within UAS platforms, subsystems, and payloads.

  • Prototyping of drones and payloads (mechanical design, electronics, systems integration).

  • Perception and machine learning for robotics.

  • Software design and development (C, C++, Python), including real-time and embedded systems.

  • UAS operations (experiments, piloting).

We furthermore expect that you publish findings at recognised international conferences and in top-ranked, peer-reviewed journals.

For certain projects and tasks at the Drone Labs at HCA Airport, a security check by relevant authorities and a driving license are required.

For further information, please contact Prof. Anders Lyhne Christensen (andc@mmmi.sdu.dk) and Associate Prof. Robert Ladig (rola@mmmi.sdu.dk).

We look forward to receiving your application.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

  • Motivated application.

  • Curriculum Vitae. 

  • Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

  • Complete list of publications.

  • Publications most relevant to the position.

  • Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

  • A research statement may be included.

  • References/reference letters may also be included.

  • A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is October 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation.

Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. jobs.title: Projektipäällikkö, kansainväliset projektit
jobs.description:
Jalo & Jalo on vuonna 1972 Turussa perustettu perheyritys, joka on erikoistunut henkilönostamiseen. Viime vuosien vahvan kasvun ja yrityskauppojen ansiosta olemme tänä päivänä Pohjoismaiden suurin nostolava-autoja vuokraava yritys.

Yrityksemme palveluksessa on yli 100 henkilönostamisen ammattilaista ja kalustossamme on 175 erilaista henkilönostinta pienistä saksilavoista suuriin nostolava-autoihin.

**Haluatko olla mukana rakentamassa ja kehittämässä kasvavaa kansainvälistä liiketoimintaa Pohjoismaissa?**

Etsimme kansainvälisiin toimintoihimme oma-aloitteista, järjestelmällistä ja tavoitteellista **projektipäällikköä** vastaamaan projektien johtamisesta, asiakassuhteiden kehittämisestä sekä liiketoiminnan kasvattamisesta erityisesti Ruotsin ja Norjan markkinoilla sekä tarvittaessa Baltian alueella.

Tarjoamme mahdollisuuden päästä mukaan kehittämään kansainvälistä liiketoimintaa yrityksessä, jolla on jo vahva perusta, olemassa oleva asiakaskunta ja toimivat prosessit. Et aloita työtä tyhjältä pöydältä, vaan pääset rakentamaan tulevaisuutta olemassa olevan pohjan päälle yhdessä kokeneen ja sitoutuneen tiimin kanssa.

Työskentelet tiiviissä yhteistyössä asiakkaiden, viranomaisten, yhteistyökumppaneiden sekä oman organisaatiomme operatiivisten toimintojen kanssa. Tehtävä edellyttää aktiivista otetta, kykyä hallita laajoja kokonaisuuksia sekä halua matkustaa Pohjoismaissa.

**Tehtävänkuva**

Projektipäällikkönä vastaat muun muassa:

- projektien myynnistä ja asiakkuuksien kehittämisestä

- projektien suunnittelusta, käynnistämisestä ja johtamisesta

- tarjouslaskennan ja sopimusneuvotteluiden tukemisesta

- kansainvälisten projektien lupa- ja viranomaisasioiden koordinoinnista

- resurssien suunnittelusta yhteistyössä toimipisteiden ajojärjestelyn kanssa

- projektien aikataulujen, kustannusten ja laadun seurannasta

- yhteistyöstä asiakkaiden, viranomaisten, alihankkijoiden ja muiden sidosryhmien kanssa

- uusien liiketoimintamahdollisuuksien tunnistamisesta ja kehittämisestä


**Odotamme sinulta**

- tehtävään soveltuvaa koulutusta ja/tai työkokemuksen kautta hankittua osaamista

- kokemusta projektijohtamisesta tai esihenkilötehtävistä ja liiketoiminnan kehittämisestä

- kykyä johtaa useita samanaikaisia projekteja tavoitteellisesti ja järjestelmällisesti

- vahvoja organisointi-, yhteistyö- ja neuvottelutaitoja

- sujuvaa suomen ja englannin kielen taitoa

- valmiutta matkustaa Pohjoismaissa ja tarvittaessa Baltian alueella

- kykyä toimia itsenäisesti, ottaa vastuuta ja tehdä päätöksiä muuttuvissa tilanteissa

- hyviä tietoteknisiä valmiuksia sekä kykyä omaksua uusia järjestelmiä ja toimintamalleja

- halua kehittää sekä omaa osaamistasi että yrityksen toimintaa pitkäjänteisesti


**Arvostamme erityisesti**

- ruotsin kielen taitoa, joka katsotaan eduksi

- kokemusta kansainvälisestä liiketoiminnasta tai projektitoiminnasta

- Pohjoismaisten markkinoiden, toimintatapojen ja viranomaisvaatimusten tuntemusta

- kokemusta teollisuuden, energiateollisuuden, infrastruktuurin tai rakennusalan projekteista

- näyttöjä asiakassuhteiden rakentamisesta ja uusien liiketoimintamahdollisuuksien tunnistamisesta

- yrittäjähenkistä, ratkaisukeskeistä ja tavoitteellista työotetta


**Henkilönä olet**

- itseohjautuva ja aloitteellinen

- luotettava ja vastuuntuntoinen

- tuloshakuinen, mutta pitkäjänteinen

- rohkea tarttumaan uusiin mahdollisuuksiin

- hyvä tiimipelaaja, joka osaa toimia eri sidosryhmien kanssa kansainvälisessä toimintaympäristössä


**Tarjoamme**

- vastuullisen ja monipuolisen tehtävän kasvavassa yrityksessä

- mahdollisuuden vaikuttaa kansainvälisen liiketoiminnan kehittämiseen

- mielenkiintoisia projekteja Pohjoismaissa ja Baltian alueella

- osaavan organisaation tuen ja matalan hierarkian työyhteisön

jobs.title: Bli BPA-assistent for blid og sporty student i Bergen
jobs.description:
Jeg er en blid, ung mann med glimt i øyet på snart 21 år som søker etter assistenter. Jeg går på 3. året på NHH, og trenger transport til og fra skolen. Rullestolen min bruker jeg ofte på tur, men jeg går også en del. Jeg er en sosial gutt og liker å være med venner på fritiden, og i den anledning trenger jeg assistanse med kjøring til og fra. Jeg er også glad i å dra på treningssenteret. Jeg bor sentralt i Bergen sammen med familien min.

Jeg ser etter tilkallingsassistenter på dag/kveld/helg. Menn i alderen 20-30 oppfordres til å søke på stillingen, men alle søknader vil bli vurdert. Dette er en stilling som passer godt for studenter, da det er mange muligheter for å studere på jobb. Ønsket oppstart er snarest, og søknader behandles fortløpende!

Jeg ser etter deg som er:

  • Snill, omtenksom og ærlig

  • Positiv/har godt humør

  • Praktisk anlagt

  • Løsningsorientert

  • Rolig og trygg

  • God fysisk form og glad i trening - ikke et krav, men vil være en fordel

Arbeidsoppgaver:

  • Forflytning

  • Kjøre meg til og fra studiested

  • Kjøre meg til og fra sosiale aktiviteter

  • Bistå med matlaging

  • Bistå med trening/tøying

  • Bistå med personlig, ikke-intimt, stell

  • Være tilgjengelig for meg

  • Helgevakter etter hvert

Kvalifikasjoner:

  • Over 20 år

  • Gode kommunikasjonsevner på norsk

  • Godkjent politiattest

  • Førerkort klasse B (manuelt gir)


Hvorfor skal du velge Humana?

Hos Humana er du mer enn bare en ansatt. Vi er opptatt av din trivsel, og du får god oppfølging fra dag én. Du blir en del av et støttende assistent-team, og vi tilbyr både veiledning og kurs for at du skal lykkes i jobben.

Dette er noe av det du får ved å jobbe hos oss:

  • Tarifflønn, ansiennitetsregulert

  • Gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger

  • Veiledning og opplæring

  • Assistentkurs i regi av Humana Omsorg og Assistanse

  • Egen app for håndbøker og rutiner

  • Rabatter hos bl.a. SATS og MOVA

  • Attraktive rabatter med fordelsprogrammet Visma LogBuy

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Humana omsorg og assistanse utvikler og leverer omsorgs- og assistansetjenester etter enkeltmenneskers behov og samfunnets ønsker. Vi yter tjenester innenfor områdene helse og omsorg, brukerstyrt personlig assistanse, barnevern institusjon og fosterhjem, praktisk bistand og hjelpetiltak.

Vi er et av Norges største private helseforetak, og vi arbeider etter visjonen, Alle har rett til et godt liv.

jobs.title: Butiksekspedient til Stormgade – fleksibelt job
jobs.description:
Har du lyst til et job, hvor du møder glade mennesker, får ansvar og bliver en del af den gode energi i vores butik på Stormgade i Hvide Sande?

Butikken er et samlingspunkt for både lokale og turister – især i højsæsonen, hvor der er masser af liv. Men vi har også brug for ekstra hænder uden for sæsonen, og derfor søger vi lige nu flere kollegaer, der har lyst til at være en del af holdet.

 

Vi søger dig, der kan arbejde:

  • Efter skole

  • I weekender

  • På hverdage

  • Eller en blanding – alt efter hvad der passer dig og vores behov

Timeantallet kan variere, og du behøver ikke kunne arbejde et bestemt antal timer. Det kan være for en kortere periode, eller noget der fortsætter, hvis det fungerer godt for os begge. Som alle andre steder er der færre timer efter uge 43 – så jobbet passer perfekt til dig, der studerer eller har et andet job ved siden af.

 

Dine opgaver

  • Betjening og ekspedition af kunder

  • Hjælp og vejledning om vores produkter

  • Opfyldning af varer og let rengøring

  • At skabe god stemning og sikre, at kunderne går herfra med en positiv oplevelse

 

Vi håber, at du

  • er imødekommende og har lyst til at tale med mennesker

  • trives i en hverdag, hvor der sker noget

  • taler og forstår dansk (engelsk/tysk er et plus, men ikke et krav)

  • er klar på at lære – erfaring er ikke nødvendig, vi sørger for oplæring

 

Arbejdstid

Ligger inden for butikkens åbningstider (kl. 6–19). Det er et stort plus, hvis du er frisk om morgenen – vores første kunder kommer allerede kl. 6 og de elsker et smil fra morgenstunden.

 

Vi tilbyder

  • Fleksible arbejdstider

  • Et godt team og en hverdag med fart på

  • Oplæring, så du føler dig tryg i opgaverne

 

Løn

Efter gældende overenskomst og dine kvalifikationer.

 

Lyder det som noget for dig?

Vi holder løbende samtaler – så send din ansøgning hurtigst muligt til:

HR@ejvinds.dk Att.: Camilla Glistrup Lauridsen

jobs.title: Pedagogisch medewerker Kinderdagverblijf
jobs.description:
Grensarbeid zoekt voor de kinderopvang Samen Spelen een pedagogisch medewerker.

Binnen Maastricht hebben we op verschillende plekken een kinderdagverblijf, opvang van 0-4 jaar. Hier hebben wij horizontale groepen en enkele verticale groepen. Specifiek voor het KDV zoeken wij pedagogisch medewerkers. Lijkt het je leuk om met deze doelgroep te werken, aarzel dan niet om te solliciteren!

Werktijden: De openingstijden zijn van 7.30-18.00 uur. De starttijd van medewerkers ligt tussen 7.30-09.00 uur en de eindtijd tussen 17.00-18.00 uur. De ene dag start je als eerste en de andere dag eindig je als laatste. Dit is opgenomen in het rooster en is tijdig bekend en wekelijks hetzelfde. De meeste groepen zijn horizontaal, er is 1 verticale groep. Je mag je voorkeur aangeven maar de keuze voor een verticale groep is beperkt.

Wij zijn op zoek naar:

  • Iemand die tussen de 18 en 32 uur per week wil werken
  • Bij voorkeur iemand die over een VVE certificaat en taalniveau 3F beschikt
  • Iemand die minimaal een MBO-niveau 4 diploma heeft
  • Iemand die bij voorkeur ervaring in de kinderopvang heeft

Wie past er bij ons?

  • Een collega die een nieuwe uitdaging aan durft te gaan.
  • Een collega die zijn/haar ervaring kan bijdragen in ons team.
  • Een collega die het leuk vindt om mee te bouwen en -werken aan inclusieve kinderopvang en integrale kindcentra.
  • Een collega die enthousiasme brengt binnen ons team.

Taalvereisten Nederlands

Kinderopvang (0–4 jaar): Nederlands niveau 3F

Buitenschoolse opvang (BSO): Nederlands niveau 2F

Sommige opleidingen voldoen hier automatisch aan. Indien nodig kan je een aanvullende cursus of taaltoets volgen — wij denken hierin actief met je mee.

Buitenlandse (incl. Belgische) diploma’s worden beoordeeld via DUO (NL). Omdat België een EU-lidstaat is, kun je in Nederland werken met je Belgische diploma — maar je moet het eerst laten erkennen. Dit heet een erkenning van beroepskwalificatie voor de functie “beroepskracht kinderopvang” (dagopvang, buitenschoolse opvang, gastouderopvang) bij DUO (NL). De procedure duurt gemiddeld ongeveer 3 weken. Erkenning of melding is gratis. Wij begeleiden je stap voor stap door het volledige traject.

jobs.title: Word Begeleider via ons Werken-Leren Traject
jobs.description:
Droom jij van een baan waar je van betekenis bent? Een baan waar jij het verschil maakt? Heb jij er ooit aan gedacht om jouw talent in een andere sector in te zetten? Dan is werken als begeleider in de gehandicaptenzorg wellicht iets voor jou. Kom alles te weten over de vacature, wie Tragel is, waar we voor staan en kom bij ons werken.

Wat ga je doen?

Bij Tragel zijn we op zoek naar verschillende type begeleiders. Afhankelijk van jouw:

  • talenten (bijvoorbeeld: je blijft rustig ook wanneer er iemand tegen je roept).
  • interesses (bijvoorbeeld: je hebt een sterke drang om mensen altijd te helpen).
  • en eventuele eerdere werkervaringen (bijvoorbeeld: bij de politie, in de beveiliging, als maatschappelijk werker of in de horeca).

Wat heb je nodig?

Om in de zorg voor mensen met een beperking aan de slag te gaan, moet je naast een hart voor de zorg hebben ook stevig in je schoenen staan. Je krijgt te maken met onverwachte situaties. Samen met je collega’s weet je van aanpakken. Samen ga je voor oplossingen! Je hebt oog voor detail en een sterk verantwoordelijkheidsgevoel. Jouw interesse voor de wereld van je cliënten en hoe zij dingen beleven houdt je scherp. Je bent flexibel, want een dag is vaak niet te plannen. Dat je goed met mensen kunt omgaan, is vereiste nummer 1. Je ziet wat je cliënten nodig hebben, ondersteunt ze en beweegt met ze mee.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral researcher position on monitoring tools for assessing animal health and welfare at the Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, Aarhus University
jobs.employer: Technical Sciences - Institut for Husdyr- og Veter
jobs.description:
We are seeking a motivated postdoctoral researcher to join our international team working on monitoring animal health and welfare.

The position is for two years and will commence December 1, 2026, or soon thereafter. The position is within the research section Management and Modelling.

The research section Management and Modelling develop methods and tools for herd management to promote animal welfare, green transition, and economic viability. Further, the section integrates, develops, and disseminates knowledge of farm animal management and relationships between actors and animals. Researchers in the section teach BSc, MSc and PhD in animal and veterinary science educations and conduct research-based public advice for national and international authorities on animal welfare and health.

The research section is a dynamic multidisciplinary research group including animal scientists, veterinarians, economists, statisticians, and anthropologists.

The position

We seek a post doc to evaluate data and monitoring tools for assessing animal health and welfare in all major livestock production systems (cattle, pig and poultry). The post doc will contribute to identification of animal-based indicators for pig welfare to be used in pig welfare inspection. The post doc will also contribute to the development of training materials in targeting pig welfare inspectors in EU member states.

Your profile

We are looking for a candidate who:
  • Holds a PhD or equivalent academic qualifications.
  • Has research experience in monitoring animal welfare, health or production on any of the major livestock production systems (cattle, pigs or poultry).

Research tasks
  • Evaluating data and monitoring tools for assessing animal health and welfare in cattle, pig or poultry
  • Identification of animal-based indicators for pig welfare to be used in screening of pig welfare in relation to inspection
  • Development and evaluation of training and testing programmes targeting European pig welfare inspectors

The preferred candidate will also engage in and further develop ongoing research and teaching within the Management and Modelling group.

What we offer
  • A well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment and animal-experimental facilities
  • An informal and multicultural research environment with high professionalism and close collaboration and networking activities
  • A workplace characterized by equality and a good work-life balance, and an open discussion across different fields of research.

Who we are

Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences is well-known for its skilled and very innovative interdisciplinary research environments with high international impact. We perform world-class research, which contributes with solutions to solve essential societal challenges within the green transition: food production and veterinary medicine – nationally and globally.

The department generates novel research at the highest international level within sustainable food production, environment, climate, and health and welfare for animals and humans. The activities form the basis for the research-based public sector consultancy and degree programs covering bachelor’s, master’s and PhD degree programs within animal science and veterinary medicine. We offer a lively, engaged and innovative learning and study environment, which is closely integrated in the research environment.

ANIVET has unique and advanced animal experimental research facilities and technologies, situated in close connection to the research environment, and a comprehensive national and international research network and good industrial and professional collaboration.

Please refer to Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences (au.dk) for further
information about the department; https://anivet.au.dk/en

Contact

Further information on the position may be obtained from Head of Research Unit, Professor Jan Tind Sørensen, phone: +4520783343, email: jantind.sorensen@anivet.au.dk.

Living in Denmark

Please visit the international staff website: https://internationalstaff.au.dk/prearrival/ for information about arriving to and living in Denmark for both the applicants and their potential family.

Place of employment and place of work

The place of work is the Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, AU Viborg, Blichers Allé 20, DK-8830 Tjele, and the area of employment is Aarhus University (AU) with related departments.


Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.


Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Why Seco?
